title: 2.5.22 When Does finally Run?
description: Build a try/catch/finally and confirm finally runs in both the success and the failure case. Auto-graded.
sourceRef: designed: practice for 2.5.5 Concepts in Practice 'When finally runs'

steps.title: Predict first
steps.instructions: In a comment, predict which blocks run when the try block succeeds: try and catch, try and finally, or all three.

steps.title: Build the success case
steps.instructions: Write a try block that logs "Work done." with no error. Give it a catch block that logs "Handling error." and a finally block that logs "Cleanup ran."

steps.title: Confirm
steps.instructions: Run it. Confirm catch was skipped but finally still ran.

requirements.title: try/catch/finally present
requirements.description: Code has a try, catch, and finally block. Help: 2.5.21 (Cleaning Up with finally)

requirements.title: try block cannot fail
requirements.description: The try block logs Work done. with nothing that can error. Help: 2.5.21 (Cleaning Up with finally)

requirements.title: finally logs cleanup
requirements.description: The finally block logs Cleanup ran. Help: 2.5.21 (Cleaning Up with finally)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.5.22 When Does finally Run?". The task they were given: In a comment, predict which blocks run when the try block succeeds: try and catch, try and finally, or all three. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
